That is deliberate and it is not a demotion of the github rule - it is the same rule applied harder. flatstack points at a service on the WINDOWS HOST, so it is unreachable whenever that host process is not running (a reboot before the scheduled task fires, a crash, a manual stop). It is therefore the entry MOST likely to fail its handshake, and the cascade only kills entries that come AFTER the failure. Last position costs nothing when flatstack is down; putting it before github would let a stopped host service take github's 47 tools with it. The residual accepted risk is the reverse direction: a github 401 would now also kill flatstack's 3 tools. That is the cheaper of the two failures.
